JSX: JSX is a syntax extension for JavaScript that looks like HTML and is compiled to React.createElement calls. It allows writing UI components declaratively in React Native.
Components: Components are reusable building blocks in React Native, defined as functions returning JSX. They accept props and manage their own state using hooks.
StyleSheet: StyleSheet provides a way to define styles with performance benefits through abstraction. It validates and optimizes style objects, and styles are only sent to native once.
Expo CLI: Expo is the recommended framework for building React Native apps. It provides managed workflows, over-the-air updates, and access to native APIs without Xcode or Android Studio.

npx create-expo-app my-app
cd my-app
npx expo start
# Press i for iOS, a for Android, w for web

View: View is the fundamental container component supporting flexbox layout, styling, touch handling, and accessibility. It maps to UIView on iOS and View on Android.
Text: Text is the only component that renders text in React Native. It supports nesting, styling, and event handling like onPress.
Image: Image displays images from local assets, network URLs, or data URIs. It requires explicit dimensions when loading from network sources.
ScrollView: ScrollView is a scrolling container for multiple components and views. It loads all content upfront and is best for smaller amounts of content.
Pressable: Pressable is the modern touch handling component that provides feedback for different press states. Use instead of TouchableOpacity for more control.

<Pressable onPress={handlePress} style={({ pressed }) => [{ opacity: pressed ? 0.5 : 1 }]}>
  <Text>Press me</Text>
</Pressable>
Modal & StatusBar: Modal presents content on top of the app, useful for alerts and forms. StatusBar controls the device status bar appearance per screen.

React Navigation: React Navigation is the standard navigation library for React Native apps, providing stack, tab, and drawer navigators with native transitions.
Stack: Stack navigator manages a navigation stack where screens are pushed and popped. It provides native-like transitions and header customization.
Tab: Tab navigator provides bottom or top tab navigation with icons and labels. Each tab maintains its own navigation state for independent back stacks.
Drawer: Drawer navigator creates a side menu that slides in from the left, supporting nested navigators and custom drawer content.
Expo Router: Expo Router provides file-based routing similar to Next.js. Files in the app/ directory automatically become routes with support for layout files and deep linking.

Fabric: Fabric is the new rendering system that uses JSI (JavaScript Interface) instead of the Bridge. It enables synchronous communication and better performance for UI updates.
TurboModules: TurboModules replace the old Native Modules system, allowing lazy loading of native modules and efficient type-safe communication via JSI.
JSI: JavaScript Interface (JSI) enables direct, synchronous communication between JavaScript and native code without the Bridge. It eliminates the serialization overhead of the old architecture.

useState: useState is a React hook that adds local state to functional components, returning a state variable and a setter function.

const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
<Button title="Press" onPress={() => setCount(count + 1)} />
AsyncStorage: AsyncStorage is an unencrypted, asynchronous key-value storage system for persisting data across app restarts on both iOS and Android.
Zustand: Zustand is a minimal state management library with a hook-based API. It works well in React Native for global state without boilerplate.
MMKV Storage: MMKV is a fast, synchronous key-value storage by Tencent. It's significantly faster than AsyncStorage and ideal for performance-critical persistence.

Animated API: React Native's built-in Animated API provides declarative animations using Animated.Value and timing/spring configurations. It drives animations natively on the UI thread.
Reanimated: Reanimated provides gesture-driven animations that run entirely on the UI thread using worklets. It enables smooth 60fps animations for complex interactions.
Gesture Handler: Gesture Handler replaces PanResponder with native gesture processing. It supports pan, pinch, rotation, tap, long press, and custom gesture compositions.

fetch: The Fetch API provides a native way to make HTTP requests in React Native. It returns promises and supports JSON, text, and binary responses.
Axios: Axios is a promise-based HTTP client with interceptors, automatic JSON parsing, and request cancellation. It provides a cleaner API than fetch.
React Query: React Query (TanStack Query) manages server state with automatic caching, refetching, pagination, and optimistic updates.
WebSocket: WebSocket enables full-duplex real-time communication over a persistent TCP connection, ideal for chat apps, live updates, and gaming.

const ws = new WebSocket('ws://example.com/socket');
ws.onmessage = (e) => console.log(e.data);

Camera: React Native Camera provides device camera access with support for photos, videos, barcode scanning, and custom camera UI.

import { Camera } from 'react-native-camera';
<Camera ref={ref => setCamera(ref)} type={Camera.Constants.Type.back} />
Location: Geolocation APIs provide device location through GPS or network positioning, supporting high-accuracy and background location tracking.
Push Notifications: Push notifications allow sending alerts to user devices even when the app is closed. Firebase Cloud Messaging is the standard solution.

import messaging from '@react-native-firebase/messaging';
const token = await messaging().getToken();

FlatList: FlatList efficiently renders large lists by virtualizing rows, recycling components, and rendering only visible items. It supports headers, footers, and pull-to-refresh.
Optimization: React Native optimization includes using PureComponent, useMemo, avoiding inline functions in render, and minimizing re-renders with React.memo.
Hermes: Hermes is an open-source JavaScript engine optimized for React Native, reducing app startup time, memory usage, and APK/IPA size.
InteractionManager: InteractionManager schedules tasks to run after animations or navigation transitions complete, preventing dropped frames during critical UI updates.

Skia: React Native Skia provides a high-performance 2D graphics canvas for custom drawing, image manipulation, and complex animations using the Skia graphics library.

import { Canvas, Circle, Group } from '@shopify/react-native-skia';

<Canvas style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  <Circle cx={100} cy={100} r={40} color='blue' />
</Canvas>
CodePush: CodePush enables over-the-air JavaScript bundle updates without going through the App Store review process, allowing instant bug fixes and small feature updates.
AppState: AppState tracks whether the app is in foreground, background, or inactive state. Use it to pause/resume timers, network requests, and animations.

iOS: iOS deployment requires an Apple Developer account, Xcode configuration, and provisioning profiles. The app is archived and uploaded via Xcode or Transporter.
Android: Android deployment generates a signed APK or AAB using keystore credentials. The build is created with Gradle and uploaded to the Play Console.
EAS Build: Expo Application Services (EAS) Build compiles and signs your app in the cloud without requiring Xcode or Android Studio installed locally.

npm install -g eas-cli
eas login
eas build --platform all
eas submit --platform ios

Navigation & Deep Linking: React Navigation is the standard navigation library. Stack, Tab, Drawer, and native stack navigators. Deep linking maps URL schemes to screens (myapp://product/123 or universal links). Linking configuration registers URL patterns. Push notifications trigger navigation via deep links. NavigationContainer handles linking. useLinkProps creates accessible links. useLinkTo navigates programmatically. Auth flow: conditional navigation based on auth state. Screen tracking for analytics via onStateChange. Screen focus detection with useFocusEffect.
React Native Animations & Gestures: React Native provides multiple animation systems: Animated (imperative), react-native-reanimated (runs on UI thread for 60fps), react-native-gesture-handler (native gesture processing). Reanimated 3 uses worklets (JS functions that run on the UI thread). Shared values, animations, and gestures compose for smooth interactions. Layout Animations for enter/exit transitions. GestureDetector for pan, pinch, tap, rotation. runOnJS calls JS thread from worklets. Skia (react-native-skia) for custom drawing and animations.
